newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: ARA bunkers steady, falls elsewhere draw buyers.
newsitem.headline: ARA bunkers steady, falls elsewhere draw buyers.

text.p: ARA fuel oil bunker prices were steady on Thursday and Hamburg prices rose, but softness elsewhere drew a few buyers, dealers said.
Rotterdam 380 cst traded at around $115 fob for late September delivery and at $116/$117 for early October, reflecting a tighter market expected at the start of next month.
Some bullish barge players reported large traded volumes in the bunker market, but most independent players said there were just a few small enquiries.
"It's not a terrible day, but the volumes are nowhere near what some people are saying," one dealer said.
Hamburg prices rose sharply to $120/$124 delivered which deterred all but the most desperate of buyers.
In contrast with the north, Mediterranean prices dipped as ports competed for lively but limited business. Dealers said trading in southern France was active, but other areas lost out.
Further east, Egyptian prices waned with demand light, but buyers were not drawn back to the market.
Durban fuel oil was still in short supply, resulting in prices of $132/$133 for 180 cst. However, suppliers expected the shortage to ease by early October and prices to fall by $10.
